title: English Subject-Verb Agreement Question Bank - Part 2
subject: English

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Two miles beyond / (b) that pasture was seen hundreds / (c) of cattle including / (d) some lambs. / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject 'hundreds of cattle' is plural, so the verb must be plural. 'was seen' should be 'were seen'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) It is noticed that / (b) the elite class have no soft / (c) corner for the downtrodden who are the / (d) real victims of the present social set-up. / (e) No Error.
options: the elite class have no soft
corner for the downtrodden who are the
real victims of the present social set-up.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Class' is a collective noun acting as a single unit here, so it takes a singular verb. 'have' should be 'has'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Ritu as well as / (b) some of her friends / (c) have fallen in love with Sonu, who / (d) is the eldest son of an S. D. O. / (e) No Error.
options: have fallen in love with Sonu, who
is the eldest son of an S. D. O.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject. 'Ritu' is singular, so 'have fallen' should be 'has fallen'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) More than one successful candidate / (b) have taken the interview for one / (c) of the popular magazines / (d) being published from Delhi. / (e) No Error.
options: have taken the interview for one
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'More than one' is always followed by a singular noun and takes a singular verb. 'have taken' should be 'has taken'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Is there any difficulties / (b) in disposing of this gorgeous building / (c) built on such a spacious / (d) and beautiful campus. / (e) No Error.
options: in disposing of this gorgeous building
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Is' is singular, so the noun must be singular. 'difficulties' should be 'difficulty'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The leader as well as / (b) his followers are fatally injured in / (c) the train accident which occured last night / (d) near this railway crossing. / (e) No Error.
options: his followers are fatally injured in
the train accident which occured last night
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: With 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('The leader', singular). 'are' should be 'is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The request of the workers' / (b) union that their wages should be / (c) increased were supported by / (d) a vast majority. / (e) No Error.
options: union that their wages should be
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'The request' (singular). 'were supported' should be 'was supported'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Along the northern forntier / (b) of India is seen / (c) the Himalayas mighty / (d) in their splendour. / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'The Himalayas' is a plural proper noun, so it requires a plural verb. 'is seen' should be 'are seen'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The publisher says / (b) that there is / (c) many important details to attend / (d) to before this book gets printed. / (e) No Error.
options: to before this book gets printed.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject 'details' is plural, so the verb must be plural. 'there is' should be 'there are'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) His politics is not / (b) good, so we have suggested to him / (c) that he should read Gandhi, Nehru / (d) and Karl Marx. / (e) No Error.
options: good, so we have suggested to him
that he should read Gandhi, Nehru
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When 'politics' refers to political principles or views, it is treated as plural. 'is not' should be 'are not'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Just outside / (b) the hotel is / (c) two bars, extremely beautiful / (d) as well as crowdy. / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject 'two bars' is plural, so the verb must be plural. 'is' should be 'are'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) We should not forget that / (b) we have a right to criticise but / (c) at the same time each of us / (d) have to remember the duty also. / (e) No Error.
options: we have a right to criticise but
at the same time each of us
have to remember the duty also.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it requires a singular verb. 'have to remember' should be 'has to remember'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Her pugnacious daughter / (b) always do something that may incur insult / (c) on her neighbours who hold a wrong / (d) opinion about her family. / (e) No Error.
options: always do something that may incur insult
on her neighbours who hold a wrong
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Daughter' is singular, so the verb must be singular. 'do' should be 'does'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) One of / (b) the biggest industrial houses / (c) in Mumbai is on the verge of / (d) declaring a lock out. / (e) No Error.
options: in Mumbai is on the verge of
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'One' is the singular subject, correctly taking the singular verb 'is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Our Head of the Department assured / (b) us that a series of lectures on Milton / (c) were to be arranged / (d) the following week and so we should not create any nuissance. / (e) No Error.
options: Our Head of the Department assured
us that a series of lectures on Milton
the following week and so we should not create any nuissance.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'a series' (singular), not 'lectures'. 'were to be arranged' should be 'was to be arranged'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) A body of volunteers / (b) have been organized / (c) to help the faculty members / (d) in their attempt to raise the funds. / (e) No Error.
options: in their attempt to raise the funds.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'A body' is a collective noun acting as a single unit, so it takes a singular verb. 'have been' should be 'has been'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Each of the students, / (b) whom I have chosen to take part / (c) in the cultural programmes to be performed / (d) in the City Hall, are up to the mark. / (e) No Error.
options: whom I have chosen to take part
in the cultural programmes to be performed
in the City Hall, are up to the mark.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the verb must be singular. 'are up' should be 'is up'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Everybody among the businessmen / (b) were enjoying drinking / (c) when the Manager of the hotel / (d) was shot dead. / (e) No Error.
options: when the Manager of the hotel
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Everybody' is singular and requires a singular verb. 'were enjoying' should be 'was enjoying'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Most of the news / (b) pertaining to the sudden demise of Dr. Sen / (c) have been communicated by some of the ruffians / (d) whom I know well. / (e) No Error.
options: pertaining to the sudden demise of Dr. Sen
have been communicated by some of the ruffians
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb. 'have been' should be 'has been'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Although these building are / (b) in need of repair, / (c) there have been much improvement / (d) in their appearance. / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Improvement' is singular, so the verb must be singular. 'have been' should be 'has been'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) He often says that / (b) it are these obscene films / (c) that lead the youth to their moral degradation / (d) and are responsible for many evils growing in our society. / (e) No Error.
options: that lead the youth to their moral degradation
and are responsible for many evils growing in our society.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'it' is singular and requires a singular verb. 'are' should be 'is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Not only the doctor / (b) but also the nurses of this nursing / (c) home is very kind and helpful / (d) to the attendants. / (e) No Error.
options: but also the nurses of this nursing
home is very kind and helpful
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: With 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it ('nurses', plural). 'is' should be 'are'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) There appears / (b) a number of new faces in the hall / (c) and I really do not know where they have / (d) come from and why. / (e) No Error.
options: a number of new faces in the hall
and I really do not know where they have
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'A number of' is always followed by a plural noun and takes a plural verb. 'appears' should be 'appear'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The teachers face the / (b) same problems in their day to day lives / (c) as do an ordinary man / (d) of our society. / (e) No Error.
options: same problems in their day to day lives
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'An ordinary man' is singular, so the verb must be singular. 'do' should be 'does'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The man who cannot / (b) believe his senses and the man who cannot / (c) believe anything else are / (d) insane. / (e) No Error.
options: believe his senses and the man who cannot
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. Two singular subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb ('are').

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The available statistics / (b) indicate that the population of the world will double in about 30 years / (c) and human life will become / (d) more and more miserable. / (e) No Error.
options: indicate that the population of the world will double in about 30 years
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Statistics' meaning numerical data is plural and correctly takes 'indicate'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Shingles are a disease / (b) in which the patient develops / (c) lots of inflamed spots round the / (d) waist. / (e) No Error.
options: lots of inflamed spots round the
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Names of diseases ending in 's' (like shingles, measles) are singular. 'are' should be 'is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) What were once glorious forts / (b) are now nothing / (c) but piles of / (d) rubble. / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'What' refers to 'forts' (plural), so the plural verbs 'were' and 'are' are correct.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Whether you should get married / (b) now or whether you should remain / (c) single all your life / (d) are your personal problem. / (e) No Error.
options: now or whether you should remain
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Two 'whether' clauses joined by 'or' represent a single alternative or choice, so they take a singular verb. 'are' should be 'is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Each faculty member as / (b) well as most of the students / (c) were of the view that there should / (d) be many more new courses in this college. / (e) No Error.
options: well as most of the students
were of the view that there should
be many more new courses in this college.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: With 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('Each faculty member', singular). 'were' should be 'was'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Does his daily struggle / (b) for existence leave time / (c) to ponder over / (d) international affairs? / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Struggle' is singular and correctly takes 'Does'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Either the manager / (b) or his assistants always try to misguide the public / (c) regarding the vacancy / (d) in the factory. / (e) No Error.
options: or his assistants always try to misguide the public
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. With 'Either...or', the verb agrees with the nearest subject ('assistants', plural), so 'try' is correct.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Every man and woman / (b) of the village have come out / (c) to see this strange child / (d) who claims to know everything about his pre-natal existence. / (e) No Error.
options: of the village have come out
who claims to know everything about his pre-natal existence.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Every' makes the compound subject singular. 'have come' should be 'has come'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) In our college, it / (b) was obligatory for each of / (c) the students to buy / (d) his own instruments. / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Each' is singular and correctly takes the singular possessive 'his'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Those athletes who / (b) did not adhere to the rules of athletics / (c) was deprived of taking part / (d) in the championship. / (e) No Error.
options: did not adhere to the rules of athletics
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'athletes' (plural), so the verb must be plural. 'was deprived' should be 'were deprived'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) One of the developing or underdeveloped / (b) countries are not in favour of launching / (c) chemical warfare because it trembles / (d) to imagine its repercussions. / (e) No Error.
options: One of the developing or underdeveloped
countries are not in favour of launching
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'One' is the subject and is singular. 'are not' should be 'is not'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Not John and his friends / (b) but Mary has surreptitiously taken / (c) your photographs and sent them / (d) to her friends. / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. With 'not... but', the verb agrees with the subject after 'but' ('Mary', singular), so 'has' is correct.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) The idea of / (b) introducing genes / (c) to correct heritable and other / (d) disorders are revolutionary. / (e) No Error.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'The idea' (singular). 'are revolutionary' should be 'is revolutionary'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) An ability to shrink / (b) and reduce oneself to a tiny form and reverse the process whenever desired / (c) belongs to the realm of fantasy and is heard of only / (d) in fairy tales or tales of magic. / (e) No Error.
options: and reduce oneself to a tiny form and reverse the process whenever desired
belongs to the realm of fantasy and is heard of only
in fairy tales or tales of magic.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'An ability' is singular and correctly takes 'belongs' and 'is'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Neither Rajni / (b) nor Ragini were to take to her heels / (c) when they saw a cobra laying / (d) at the gate. / (e) No Error.
options: nor Ragini were to take to her heels
when they saw a cobra laying
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: With 'Neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearest subject ('Ragini', singular). 'were' should be 'was'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Have either of / (b) the two candidates been / (c) selected for the post of Branch Manager / (d) in the Punjab National Bank? / (e) No Error.
options: selected for the post of Branch Manager
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Either' is singular and should take a singular verb in formal English. 'Have' should be 'Has'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) None / (b) of the five players / (c) who have been given a chance / (d) to join this team play confidently. / (e) No Error.
options: who have been given a chance
to join this team play confidently.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'None' meaning 'not one' takes a singular verb. 'play' should be 'plays'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) What she says / (b) and what she does / (c) are incomprehensible / (d) to an ordinary mind like yours. / (e) No Error.
options: to an ordinary mind like yours.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. Two 'what' clauses joined by 'and' represent distinct ideas and take a plural verb ('are').

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Where she went / (b) and where she left her purse / (c) are not known to us; so it / (d) is of no use being worried about her. / (e) No Error.
options: and where she left her purse
are not known to us; so it
is of no use being worried about her.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. Two 'where' clauses joined by 'and' represent distinct ideas and take a plural verb ('are').

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Nobody else / (b) but these comely young women have / (c) played a prank on you; but it is pitiable that you don't / (d) understand it. / (e) No Error.
options: but these comely young women have
played a prank on you; but it is pitiable that you don't
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The subject is 'Nobody' (singular). Phrases starting with 'but' do not change the number. 'have' should be 'has'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Some highly significant / (b) observations has been made by the former UN / (c) Secretary General, Mr. Perez De Cuelar, / (d) in his annual report submitted to the current session of General Assembly. / (e) No Error.
options: observations has been made by the former UN
Secretary General, Mr. Perez De Cuelar,
in his annual report submitted to the current session of General Assembly.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Observations' is plural, so the verb must be plural. 'has been' should be 'have been'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) If any proof was needed to show that the United Nations / (b) have lately become a policy tool in the hands of the U. S. A. and that / (c) the world's sole might has a subservient international body, it was provided / (d) by President Bush's angry comment. / (e) No Error.
options: If any proof was needed to show that the United Nations
have lately become a policy tool in the hands of the U. S. A. and that
the world's sole might has a subservient international body, it was provided
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'United Nations' is the name of a single organization and takes a singular verb. 'have' should be 'has'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) If Mahatma Gandhi / (b) was alive / (c) he would start weeping / (d) to see the present condition of India. / (e) No Error.
options: to see the present condition of India.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: This is a hypothetical/unreal conditional (second conditional). The verb 'be' should be 'were' for all subjects. 'was' should be 'were'.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) Was she a bird / (b) she would definitely fly to you / (c) and say that she could not / (d) live without you. / (e) No Error.
options: she would definitely fly to you
and say that she could not
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. Inverted conditional 'Was she a bird' (meaning 'If she were a bird') is a valid literary construction.

questions.q: Spot the error: (a) There were / (b) reports a few days before the Accra Session commenced / (c) that concrete measures to / (d) restructure the movement would be considered. / (e) No Error.
options: reports a few days before the Accra Session commenced
restructure the movement would be considered.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Reports' is plural and correctly takes 'were'.
